item.title: Pure-blue quantum-dot light-emitting diodes with minimal efficiency roll-off and high brightness
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02041-8 Quantum dots with compositionally graded shells enhance quantum-dot LED performance, achieving pure-blue emission with a peak external quantum efficiency of 23.8%, 95% of which is retained at a luminance of 50,000 cd m−2.

item.title: Physicist develops detector capable of counting photons for quantum computing
item.description: Detecting a single photon is a challenge in itself. But what if you also want to know exactly how many photons arrive at a particular point at the same time? Physicist Erik Baalbergen is working on light detectors that can do just that. They form a key building block for the optical quantum computer of the future.

item.title: Optical control stabilizes cold-atom comagnetometry
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02043-6 The use of tailored laser fields improves the coherence times of two co-trapped ytterbium isotopes, resulting in the rejection of magnetic-field noise by more than thirty-thousand-fold, opening the way to improved comagnetometry.

item.title: Measuring hard X-ray attosecond pulses
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02037-4 The generation and characterization of high-power X-ray attosecond pulses is a challenging research frontier in free-electron laser science. Now, researchers at the Linac Coherent Light Source have demonstrated experimental confirmation and measurement of hard X-ray pulses reaching 100-attosecond durations.

item.title: Light-matter hybrids form supersolid quantum state at room temperature
item.description: Researchers from the Faculty of Physics at the University of Warsaw, the Military University of Technology (Poland), IBM Research Zurich and the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS) have observed a new quantum state of matter known as a supersolid in an exciton-polariton Bose-Einstein condensate. Remarkably, the phenomenon occurs not at temperatures close to absolute zero, but at room temperature. The results have been published in Science Advances.

item.title: All-optical thin-film lithium niobate memristor
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02048-1 Oxygen-ion implantation allows the direct fabrication of photonic memristors in thin-film lithium niobate. The resulting devices combine 3-bit non-volatile optical memory, submicrosecond responses and femtojoule-level switching energies.

item.title: Ultrathin kagome material opens a route to study unusual quantum states
item.description: How atoms are arranged inside materials can influence the behavior of electrons and the resulting electronic states. Kagome lattices, repeating arrangements of atoms forming triangles that share corners (with hexagonal spaces between them), have been linked with the emergence of unusual electronic states.

item.title: A single measurement makes quantum bits more reliable
item.description: Researchers at the University of Regensburg and their international partners have found a way to significantly reduce errors in quantum bits. In an experiment, they demonstrated that a single additional measurement before a series of quantum operations can cut the error rate by more than half. The results have been published in Applied Physics Reviews.

item.title: Single molecules could provide the building blocks for future quantum networks
item.description: Quantum computers rely on qubits as their units of information. To connect them into a larger network across long distances, they need to transmit quantum information using light.

Quantum gas microscope reveals individual atoms in first tunable three-component Hubbard system
item.description: For the first time, an international team of researchers from Germany, Thailand, India, China and the United States has created a three-component Hubbard system with tunable interactions in the laboratory. In doing so, the team used a quantum gas microscope to make the individual atoms visible. The study, published in Science, provides an important foundation for future quantum simulations of nuclear physics and materials science.

item.title: Electrical control of an unconventional quantum transport state demonstrated in a magnet for the first time
item.description: Researchers at Tohoku University and the Japan Atomic Energy Agency (JAEA) have successfully controlled a unique quantum phenomenon—the quantum-geometric nonlinear Hall (QgNLH) state—using electric current for the first time. The breakthrough was achieved by revealing and exploiting the coupling between the spin structure and the QgNLH state in an electrically switchable chiral antiferromagnet.

item.title: A carefully timed pair of light pulses can amplify the motion of atomic layers in a quantum material
item.description: The principle "Work smarter, not harder!" apparently also applies to controlling quantum materials with light. Many of their fascinating properties depend on how the atoms are arranged in the crystal. Ultrashort laser pulses can be used to alter these structures in a targeted way—the light first excites electrons, whose changed energy and dynamics exert forces on the atomic nuclei and can thereby set the atoms in motion. item.title: Trapping quasiparticles creates quantum behaviour
item.description: New research shows that trapping spinons can create, rather than destroy, protected quantum behaviour at a material’s edges The post Trapping quasiparticles creates quantum behaviour appeared first on Physics World .

item.title: Finding the fingerprints of noisy distributions in random quantum systems
item.description: Imagine shuffling a deck of cards where some of the cards are fading just because of the way they interact with the external environment as you shuffle them. Your job is to figure out the interplay between the shuffling, or "imposed randomness," due to the way you shuffle your cards and how that relates to the fading as cards are exposed to the external environment.

item.title: Experiment supports theoretical foundation for potentially more error-resistant quantum computing
item.description: One approach to making information storage in quantum computing less prone to errors is known as topological quantum computing. It relies on special quantum states that are expected to be more resistant to local disturbances.

item.title: 四部门：推动科技保险高质量发展 在人工智能、集成电路、量子科技等领域开发专属产品
item.description: 昨日，科技部、金融监管总局、工业和信息化部、国家知识产权局联合印发《关于加快推动科技保险高质量发展 有力支撑高水平科技自立自强的若干意见》（以下简称《意见》），旨在健全重大技术攻关风险分散机制，构建覆盖科技创新全链条、全周期的科技保险政策体系。

item.title: 工信部召开务虚会 研究谋划“十五五”及开局之年工作：以综合整治“内卷式”竞争为重点
item.description: 2025年12月7日，工业和信息化部党组书记、部长李乐成主持召开务虚会，深入学习贯彻党的二十届四中全会精神，研究谋划“十五五”及开局之年工作思路和举措。部领导辛国斌、叶民、张云明、熊继军、柯吉欣、单忠德、谢远生、张建民、高东升、谢少锋、钟志红出席会议，结合分管领域工作逐一发言，交流学习体会，分析研判当前形势，提出意见建议。
